rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the six-peak elution window while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. This establishes the critical pairs and a baseline for subsequent slope and temperature adjustments.

The maximum CRF is already achieved, so test a shorter gradient to reduce run time while retaining full resolution. Keeping the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed isolates slope sensitivity, with the current minimum resolution of 3.98 providing substantial margin.

Shorten the gradient another grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method while preserving the maximum CRF. The first pair is slope-sensitive but its current resolution of 2.46 leaves room for further compression.

Test whether higher temperature shortens the fastest fully resolved method without losing its maximum CRF. This also probes temperature selectivity for the critical first pair before attempting a two-minute gradient.

Higher temperature worsened the critical early pair, so test the lowest temperature to improve its selectivity while shortening the gradient to two minutes. The four-minute method at 40 C remains a fully resolved fallback with maximum CRF.

Reduce gradient steepness while retaining the favorable low temperature to lift the critical pair toward baseline resolution. The last peak will likely move into the final hold, so this tests whether a two-minute gradient can achieve maximum CRF without excessive late retention.

Shift both solvent endpoints upward while preserving the slope that resolved every pair in injection 6. The stronger final hold should accelerate the last peak, while the modest increase in starting organic tests whether early-pair resolution is retained.

Shift the same successful gradient slope upward again to shorten late retention while preserving low-temperature selectivity. The first peak should still remain retained, but its resolution will reveal whether the higher starting organic begins to compress the early pair.

Move the gradient window upward one more step at the same resolving slope, reaching the strongest available final solvent. This should shorten the last peak’s hold-phase retention while testing whether the early pair remains fully resolved.

Raise the starting organic one step to advance the last peak while making the gradient slightly shallower. Monitor the early pair closely because its first peak is approaching the weakly retained region; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-CRF method.

Increase temperature by one grid step to shorten late retention while using the early pair’s resolution margin of 1.77. This tests a modest thermal improvement without further raising the starting organic near the weak-retention boundary.

Test the next higher starting-organic setting at the temperature most favorable to the early pair. This probes the boundary for further solvent-window trimming; if weak retention erodes resolution, retain injection 11 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Back off the starting organic to avoid the early-pair compression seen at 0.35. Test a slightly shallower gradient to offset the selectivity loss at higher temperature, seeking another maximum-CRF method with rapid late elution.

Shift injection 13’s gradient window downward at unchanged slope to restore early retention and test whether the critical pair recovers full resolution. Reduce the gradient span one step to lift the critical pair from R 1.42 toward full resolution at 35 C. This should modestly delay the final peak but keep it comfortably below ten minutes, potentially restoring maximum CRF.

Return to 30 C and test a slightly shallower gradient than the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, injection 11. This should increase the critical pair’s resolution margin with only a small retention-time cost; injection 15’s rounded R of 1.50 remains marginal.

Test the next temperature step directly above the fastest fully resolved method, injection 11, to establish its speed limit. Early-pair resolution may fall below 1.5, but this checks whether the stronger endpoint can deliver a faster maximum-CRF run before retaining 30 C.

The 35 C test lost full resolution, so return to the more selective 25 C condition and slightly narrow the gradient window. This should provide more early-pair resolution margin than injection 9 while retaining a short, maximum-CRF separation.

Raise injection 18’s temperature by one step to test whether its extra early-pair margin supports faster elution while maintaining maximum CRF. This also checks a lower-starting-organic alternative to injection 11, which remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Refine around the successful low-temperature methods by reducing the final organic one step from injection 20. This tests whether a shallower gradient increases the critical-pair margin while keeping all peaks well within the maximum-CRF time window.

Raise injection 22’s temperature one step to shorten its final hold while using the critical pair’s resolution margin of 1.90. This refines a nearby maximum-CRF alternative; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
